faq: Can Squarespace import my WordPress blog?
Yes, Squarespace can import WordPress posts and pages, but the result often needs cleaning. We run the import, fix broken formatting and images, and rebuild layouts so the posts look right.
Can you move my online store to Squarespace?

Yes. Premium includes up to 100 products or posts. For larger catalogs, tell us the size and we quote the extra work. Not every platform lets customer and order history move in full, and we say what is possible up front.
Some movement is normal after a migration. We keep page addresses where possible, redirect every changed address and carry over titles and descriptions. We cannot promise rankings.
When does my old site stop working?
Only when you decide. We build on your Squarespace address first. After you approve, we point the domain to Squarespace and you cancel the old hosting yourself.

desc:
Website migration to Squarespace moves your pages, text, images and posts from another builder into one place you can edit easily. Ecom Swift LLC rebuilds your layout, sets up redirects for changed addresses and keeps your old site live until the new one is ready.

## What does website migration to Squarespace involve?

Website migration to Squarespace means moving an existing site from WordPress, Wix, Weebly or another platform into a Squarespace account. Content is copied across, pages are rebuilt in the Squarespace editor, blog posts are imported, and old addresses are pointed at their new homes.

A migration is a rebuild with a plan, because layouts and features do not transfer between platforms automatically.

## Why migrations go wrong when rushed

The common failures are quiet ones. A page is moved but its old address is not redirected, so people following an old link or a search result land on an error page. Images arrive at full size and slow the new site. Page titles are not carried over, so the pages lose the wording that search engines already know.

Switching the domain too early is another risk. If the new site is incomplete when the address changes, visitors see the gaps before you do.

## How a careful move protects traffic and leads

Search engines and visitors both remember addresses. Redirects tell them where an old page now lives, which keeps links, bookmarks and search listings useful. Carrying over titles and descriptions preserves the signals each page already has, and results after a move still depend on many factors outside our control.

A clean structure also helps visitors. A tidier menu and consistent layout make it easier to find information, and a working contact form means enquiries keep arriving through the change.

## What a good migration includes

- A page inventory listing everything that must move.
- Text and images copied and checked against the original.
- Layouts rebuilt in Squarespace to match your look or improve it.
- Blog posts imported with dates and categories where possible.
- A redirect list for every address that changes.
- Page titles and descriptions carried across.
- Contact forms and newsletter sign-ups reconnected and tested.
- Images resized, with alt text added in larger packages.
- A guide for updating Google Search Console after launch.

## How we do it

We list your pages, then build the new site privately while your current one stays online. Once everything is checked, we set up redirects and agree a switch date with you. Your domain is connected only when you approve, and we help with the steps at your domain provider.

The Basic package suits a small site of a few pages. Standard adds more pages, imported posts, tested redirects and carried-over titles. Premium moves a large site, imports many posts or products, improves menus and structure, and includes a period of follow-up fixes.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your current site live until we say the new one is ready.
- Tell us which pages are essential and which can be retired.
- Export or save copies of your old content.
- Check that you can log in to your domain provider.

**Avoid:**
- Cancelling the old site on the day of the switch.
- Changing page addresses without a redirect.
- Carrying over old pages that no longer serve a purpose.
- Expecting a store with complex features to transfer in the same way as a simple site.

## Who this is for

An owner tired of maintaining plugins wants a simpler editor. A small business on a platform that no longer fits wants a cleaner look without losing past blog content. A freelancer taking over several sites wants them in one consistent system.

## What we need from you

Send the address of your current site and tell us what to keep. We never need passwords. Give us access to the old site as a staff or admin user where the platform allows it, or send an export file. In Squarespace, invite us as a contributor with the permissions needed to build and connect the domain.
